packet.headline_seed: French national shows symptoms on return from hantavirus-hit ship
packet.description_seed: Five passengers of the MV Hondius will be quarantined in Paris "until further notice", France's prime minister says.

what: French national shows symptoms on return from hantavirus-hit ship

clean_source_blocks.text: A passenger of a cruise ship that was struck by an outbreak of hantavirus has shown symptoms of the disease while being repatriated to France, the country's prime minister has said. Sébastien Lecornu said the French national developed symptoms while on a chartered flight from Tenerife to Paris, and so all five evacuated from the MV Hondius had been "immediately placed in strict isolation until further notice". The French citizens are among more than 90 tourists to be ferried home from the Dutch vessel on Sunday, which anchored off the Canary Islands before dawn. Three passengers have died after travelling on the ship, two of whom were confirmed to have had the virus.

A French national who was evacuated from the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship, where three passengers died of the rat-borne illness, has begun experiencing symptoms of the disease, officials said Sunday. The French national, who was not publicly named, was en route to a hospital in Paris along with four others when they began to show symptoms of the hantavirus, Prime Minister Sebastian Lecornu said in a statement. As a result, all five French citizens, who were evacuated from the MV Hondius, have been placed in immediate isolation until further notice, the premier added. The sick citizen was being flown from Tenerife to Paris when the symptoms began manifesting, sparking fears of a wider outbreak as more than 20 nations seek to repatriate their citizens who were onboard the ship where the hantavirus infections emerged.
Five passengers of the MV Hondius will be quarantined in Paris "until further notice", France's prime minister says.

After the French flight touched down at Le Bourget Airport, officials wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) could be seen meeting them on the tarmac. Ambulances then took them to the Bichat hospital in the French capital. There, they will be quarantined for 72 hours and given a full assessment, before being sent home to self-isolate for 45 days, France's Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs said in a statement. Fourteen Spanish nationals flown from Tenerife to Madrid now face mandatory quarantine at a military hospital in the Spanish capital. British nationals have been flown back to Manchester. None of the Britons have reported symptoms but they are being monitored, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said. A plane carrying 26 passengers and crew - including eight Dutch nationals - has arrived in the Netherlands.

[Lähde: New York Post]
A French national who was evacuated from the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship, where three passengers died of the rat-borne illness,  has begun experiencing symptoms of the disease, officials said Sunday.

The French national, who was not publicly named, was en route to a hospital in Paris along with four others when they began to show symptoms of the hantavirus, Prime Minister Sebastian Lecornu said in a statement.

As a result, all five French citizens, who were evacuated from the MV Hondius, have been placed in immediate isolation until further notice, the premier added.

The sick citizen was being flown from Tenerife to Paris when the symptoms began manifesting, sparking fears of a wider outbreak as more than 20 nations seek to repatriate their citizens who were onboard the ship where the hantavirus infections emerged.

More than 90 tourists were ferried home from the Dutch vessel on Sunday by a team of hazmat-wearing emergency workers.

Professionals wearing similar full-body protective equipment were seen at France’s Le Bourget Airport when the five nationals landed early Sunday.

The five French citizens were loaded onto ambulances and taken to Paris’ Bichat hospital, where they will be under quarantine for three days and given a full assessment, according to France’s Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.

After the quarantine period, the French cruise passengers will be sent home to self-isolate for a total of 45 days, the ministry added.

There were also 17 Americans among the evacuated heading home for evaluation. The US nationals are bound for the National Quarantine Unit at the University of Nebraska Medical Center.

The World Health Organization has recommended a 42-day isolation period for the passengers of the ill-fated vessel, with the outbreak leading to the deaths of three people so far.

Five others from the ill-fated cruise, not counting the French national, have become seriously sick with the hantavirus, which has a 38% fatality rate.

Acting CDC Director Jay Bhattacharya downplayed fears that the isolated outbreak would result in a COVID-19-like pandemic, noting that previous outbreaks of hantavirus have been successfully contained in the past.

payload.title: Ranskalaismatkustajalla oireita hantavirusepäilyn jälkeen – MV Hondiukselta evakuoidut eristettiin Pariisissa
payload.summary: Ranskan pääministerin mukaan yksi MV Hondius -aluksella matkustanut ranskalainen sai hantavirukseen viittaavia oireita paluulennolla Teneriffalta Pariisiin. Kaikki viisi Ranskaan evakuoitua matkustajaa on asetettu tiukkaan eristykseen.
payload.content:
Yksi MV Hondius -risteilyalukselta Ranskaan evakuoitu matkustaja on saanut hantavirukseen viittaavia oireita paluulennolla Teneriffalta Pariisiin, Ranskan pääministeri Sébastien Lecornu kertoi. Tämän vuoksi kaikki viisi alukselta evakuoitua Ranskan kansalaista asetettiin välittömästi tiukkaan eristykseen Pariisissa, kun viranomaiset arvioivat heidän terveydentilaansa ja mahdollisia jatkotoimia.

## Oireet havaittiin paluulennolla

Ranskan kansalainen oli matkalla tilauslennolla Teneriffalta Pariisiin, kun oireet alkoivat ilmetä. Henkilön nimeä ei ole kerrottu julkisuuteen. Lento liittyi matkustajien kotiuttamiseen MV Hondiukselta, joka oli ollut Kanariansaarten edustalla ennen evakuointeja.

Kun ranskalaisia kuljettanut kone laskeutui Le Bourget’n lentoasemalle, suojavarusteisiin pukeutuneet viranomaiset ottivat matkustajat vastaan kenttäalueella. Matkustajat vietiin ambulansseilla Bichat’n sairaalaan Ranskan pääkaupungissa.

Ranskan ulkoministeriön mukaan viisi evakuoitua pidetään sairaalassa 72 tunnin karanteenissa, ja heille tehdään perusteellinen terveydentilan arviointi. Sen jälkeen heidän on määrä jatkaa eristäytymistä kotona 45 päivän ajan, jos viranomaiset katsovat sen mahdolliseksi.

## MV Hondiukselta kotiutetaan matkustajia

Ranskalaiset ovat osa yli 90 turistin joukkoa, joita kuljetettiin pois hollantilaisalukselta sunnuntaina. MV Hondius oli ankkuroitunut Kanariansaarten edustalle ennen aamunkoittoa, minkä jälkeen eri maiden kansalaisia alettiin palauttaa kotimaihinsa.

Aluksella matkustamisen jälkeen kolme ihmistä on kuollut. Heistä kahdella on vahvistettu olleen hantavirus. Tapaus on johtanut varotoimiin useissa maissa, kun yli 20 valtiota on järjestänyt omien kansalaistensa kotiuttamista alukselta.

## Useat maat seuraavat tilannetta

Espanjaan lennätetyt 14 kansalaista on määrätty pakolliseen karanteeniin Madridissa sijaitsevaan sotilassairaalaan. Britannian kansalaisia on puolestaan lennätetty Manchesteriin. Britannian terveysviranomaisten mukaan heillä ei ole ilmoitettu oireita, mutta heidän tilaansa seurataan.

Alankomaihin on saapunut kone, jossa oli 26 matkustajaa ja miehistön jäsentä. Heidän joukossaan oli kahdeksan Alankomaiden kansalaista. Viranomaiset seuraavat tilannetta, kun maat arvioivat mahdollisia jatkotoimia tartuntariskin rajaamiseksi.

After the French flight touched down at Le Bourget Airport, officials wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) could be seen meeting them on the tarmac. Ambulances then took them to the Bichat hospital in the French capital. There, they will be quarantined for 72 hours and given a full assessment, before being sent home to self-isolate for 45 days, France's Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs said in a statement. Fourteen Spanish nationals flown from Tenerife to Madrid now face mandatory quarantine at a military hospital in the Spanish capital. British nationals have been flown back to Manchester. None of the Britons have reported symptoms but they are being monitored, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said. A plane carrying 26 passengers and crew - including eight Dutch nationals - has arrived in the Netherlands.
